$comment: Dispositions for fenced code blocks in docs/content/docs (enforced by tests/e2e/cua-sdk/docs/extract.py --lint). Every fence carries exactly one of test="<lane>[,<lane>]" id="<id>", skip="<reason>" or output. A lane is listed here only once a runner executes it; a skip reason names its owner and, optionally, an expiry date after which the linter rejects it. Each lane names the e2e lane (tests/e2e/cua-sdk/scenarios.json) whose run must produce a result for every block tagged with it (docs-coverage).

docs.what: Python and TypeScript blocks run hermetically by tests/e2e/cua-sdk/python/test_docs_blocks.py (sessions, hidden preludes such as fakefleet)

container.what: Python / TypeScript blocks that start local sandboxes (Docker, gVisor), run by test_docs_blocks.py in the container lane

fleet.what: whole scripts against live Fleet (nightly; pools cua-e2e-<run>-docs-*)

contrib.what: Python blocks on contrib providers (on="daytona", ...) against cua-contrib-fixtures (schema mocks of the provider APIs and a mock cua-spacesd), run by test_docs_blocks.py in the contrib lane of .github/workflows/ci-cua-contrib.yml

cli-shape.what: every cua, cua-driver and lume command in the block parses against the CLI's generated definition (scripts/docs-generators/cli-specs); nothing runs

config.what: JSON, JSONC, YAML and TOML blocks parse, and validate against schema=<name> when given (tests/e2e/cua-sdk/docs/config_lane.py)

excerpt.what: the block is byte-identical to a marked region (// #region docs:<id>) of a file CI builds, named by source="<repo path>#<id>"; extract.py --lint checks it

lume.what: bash blocks run on a disposable macOS CI machine (tests/e2e/cua-sdk/docs/shell_lane.py --lane lume; nightly)

windows.what: PowerShell blocks run on a disposable Windows CI machine (tests/e2e/cua-sdk/docs/shell_lane.py --lane windows; nightly)

swift.what: Swift blocks compile against libs/cua/swift (tests/e2e/cua-sdk/docs/compile_lane.py --lane swift; compile-only)

kotlin.what: Kotlin blocks compile against libs/cua/kotlin (tests/e2e/cua-sdk/docs/compile_lane.py --lane kotlin; compile-only)

host-install.why: installs software on the reader's machine (package managers, curl | sh installers)

host-macos-permissions.why: needs macOS TCC grants (Accessibility, Screen Recording) on a real Mac

macos-vm.why: needs a macOS host with nested virtualization (nightly Lume lane)

windows-host.why: needs an interactive Windows session (nightly Windows lane)

destructive.why: deletes or overwrites user state; never run by CI

placeholder.why: a template the reader fills in; must show a visible placeholder such as <name> or ...

third-party-cli.why: drives a third-party tool or service CI cannot reach (cloud consoles, agents, editors)

pseudo.why: illustrative pseudo-code or an excerpt that is not meant to run on its own

diagram.why: a diagram (mermaid) rendered by the site, not code

legacy-frozen.why: documents a legacy surface kept for existing users; frozen until the page is retired

browser.why: runs in a web page (the wasm build); exercised by the e2e suite's playwright browser lane, not as a docs block

no-runner.why: needs a runner no docs lane has yet (a local Docker service started by hand, repository bench scripts, live media streaming, sample build steps); retag when the lane exists

live-cloud-only.why: needs something only a real cloud image serves (an image's own web display page), in a fragment of a page whose image the reader supplies. The fake Fleet of cua-test-fixtures gives every claim a cua-spacesd and the signed-URL API, so other cloud fragments run on PRs.

many-sandboxes.why: starts several desktop sandboxes at once (fan-out examples); beyond a CI runner's memory, and the single-sandbox calls it uses are tested elsewhere

cua-spaces.why: needs the Cua Spaces daemon (source-available, FSL-1.1-MIT), whose Keyvault asks the user to approve; the open source SDK lanes run without it. cua-spaces-ext's tests (spaces_daemon_boundary, e2e_teleport_app) and the binding smoke tests cover these calls through the daemon

local-vm.why: boots a local QEMU VM (bare-metal acceleration); the nightly qemu lane covers local VMs through the local-qemu scenario tests

your-cloud.why: creates billable resources in the reader's own cloud account (AWS, Google Cloud, Modal); cua-byoc's hermetic tests (a scripted cloud and the fake relay) and the manual cloud conformance suite (apps/cua-spaces-macos/scripts/reliability/cloud_suite.py) cover these calls
